h1: The 5 Best Reclining Office Chairs with Footrests of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Reclining Office Chairs: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five reclining office chairs with built-in footrests, covering weight limits, lumbar support, headrests and seat comfort.
summary: The GTPLAYER Big and Tall chair is the pick for larger users, with a 400 lb rating and a footrest that locks out. The N-GEN Gaming chair is the budget recliner with adjustable lumbar, and the GTPLAYER with headrest adds neck support for less. The Homall adds lumbar massage, and the wide teddy fleece chair suits cross-legged sitters.
intro: A footrest on an office chair sounds like a luxury until you realize how many people nap, read or take calls half-reclined at their desk. The problem is that many chairs sold with footrests have a flimsy leg support that tips the chair or collapses when you actually lean back.

We narrowed the pool to five chairs that really include a footrest, dropping the mesh and executive models that do not. They are ranked on paper by recline range, footrest design, lumbar support and weight capacity. Prices are buckets.

products.name: GTPLAYER Big and Tall Gaming Chair 400lbs Heavy Duty Office Chair with Foot Rest & Ergonomic Pocket Spring Lumbar Support
products.verdict: High weight rating, a locking footrest and near-flat recline.
products.description:
This chair has a 400 lb weight capacity, a pull-out footrest that locks extended, a pocket spring lumbar cushion, a high-back 3D saddle cushion and a near-flat recline. It is in the $100-200 bucket.

The 400 lb GTPLAYER leads the field as the weight rating and locking footrest address the two weak points of most gaming recliners. The cost is that it is the largest and priciest of the group.

Choose it if you are a larger user who wants to recline fully. Measure your room, since it takes real space when flat.
cons: Highest price of the gaming trio
products.idealFor: Larger users who want full recline.

products.name: N-GEN GAMING Video Gaming Chair with Footrest Lumbar Support for Home Office High Back Recliner
products.verdict: A real footrest and height-adjustable lumbar for less.
products.description:
The N-GEN has a pull-out footrest, height-adjustable lumbar support, a high-back recliner shape, a 360 degree swivel base and leather-look upholstery. It sits in the $50-100 bucket.

The N-GEN comes second as adjustable lumbar is rare at this price, though it gives no weight rating in the listing, unlike the GTPLAYER Big and Tall above.

It suits average-size adults who want a recliner without the premium cost. Check the weight limit on the product page.
products.skipIf: You need a stated heavy-duty rating.

products.name: GTPLAYER Gaming Chair, Computer Chair with Footrest and Lumbar Support, Height Adjustable with 360-Swivel Seat and Headrest
products.verdict: Adds an adjustable headrest to the footrest and recline.
products.description:
This GTPLAYER has a pull-out footrest, an adjustable headrest, a standard lumbar cushion, a 360 degree swivel with gas lift height adjustment and a reclining backrest. It is in the $50-100 bucket.

The headrest GTPLAYER sits third as its lumbar is a plain cushion rather than the adjustable or spring versions above, but the headrest helps when you recline to read or watch.

Best for users who spend long periods leaning back. The footrest and headrest together make it a lounge-style seat.

products.name: Homall Gaming Chair, Video Game Chair with Footrest and Massage Lumbar Support, Height Adjustable with Swivel Seat and Headrest
products.verdict: A vibrating lumbar cushion on top of recline and footrest.
products.description:
The Homall has a pull-out footrest, a vibrating massage lumbar cushion, an adjustable headrest, a height-adjustable swivel base and a reclining backrest. It is in the $50-100 bucket.

The Homall lands fourth as the massage cushion is a novelty to many users and the listing offers no structural details to set it apart from the GTPLAYER with headrest.

Best for buyers who like the idea of light lumbar vibration. Do not expect it to replace real back support.

products.name: Big and Tall Office Chair, Flip Armrests for Pets & Cross Legged Sitting, Executive Ergonomic Chair with Foot Rest, Teddy Fleece Wide Seat
products.verdict: Wide soft seat with flip-up armrests for different postures.
products.description:
This executive-style high-back chair has a wide teddy fleece seat, flip-up armrests, an included footrest and a reclining backrest. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

The teddy fleece chair ends the list as it costs the most, and the listing gives no weight rating or lumbar detail, while the GTPLAYER models cost far less. Its draw is posture flexibility.

It suits people who sit cross-legged or share the seat with a pet. Fleece may be warm in summer.

whatMatters.detail: A pull-out footrest tucks under the seat, while a locking one holds firm under your legs. A flimsy footrest wobbles when you lean back. Look for the word locks or locking in the spec bullets.
The rated limit reflects the base, gas lift and frame, not just the seat. A chair rated at 400 lbs has more margin. Always compare your weight with the stated limit.
Some chairs recline only slightly, while others go near flat. A deeper recline suits napping, but needs room behind the chair. Check the phrase near-flat or the angle in degrees.
Adjustable lumbar lets you match your back curve, while a plain cushion cannot move. Spring cushions add give. Look for adjustable or pocket spring.
A headrest matters when reclined, as your neck has nothing else to rest on. Check whether it adjusts.

faq.q: Can these chairs be used as office chairs?
faq.a: Yes. They swivel and adjust in height, though their style is more gaming than corporate.
Assuming every chair in a gaming listing includes a footrest. Mesh and executive models often do not.

faq.q: Is the 400 lb model worth it?
faq.a: Only if you need the rating or full recline. Others are fine for average builds.

faq.q: How do I set the recline?
faq.a: Use the lever beneath the seat and lock it where comfortable.

faq.q: How do I maintain the footrest?
faq.a: Check the locking mechanism periodically and avoid standing on it.
Fleece traps hair and dust, so vacuum it regularly.

finalTake: The GTPLAYER Big and Tall is the top pick for anyone who really wants to lean back. The N-GEN is the better value for average-size users. Check the footrest and weight rating before you buy.
